memory.content: All documentation entries must follow the standard format: Title, Definition, Key Attributes (bulleted list), Related Terms (links), and References section. Each entry should be concise and use industry-standard terminology.
EDI transaction documentation is top priority. All EDI documents (997, 204, 990, 850, 810) must include transaction code, purpose, business use case, and required/optional fields breakdown.
Use official industry terminology from NMFTA (National Motor Freight Traffic Association) standards and SCAC (Standard Carrier Alpha Code) guidelines. Avoid colloquial or regional terms.
Cross-reference related terms using relative markdown links. Link to parent category in each entry (e.g., LTL entries link to modes/, EDI entries link to edi/).

Knowledge base organized into 7 top-level categories: modes/ (shipping modes), edi/ (EDI transactions), terms/ (general terminology), parties/ (stakeholders), locations/ (geography), packaging/ (units), financials/ (cost structures). Each new entry must fit one category.
All documentation must be verifiable against official sources. Include reference links to NMFTA, ANSI X12, or carrier-specific documentation. No speculative or opinion-based content.

# Categories:

1. modes/ - Transportation methods (LTL, FTL, Parcel, Intermodal, Break Bulk, Air, Ocean)
2. edi/ - EDI transaction sets (997, 204, 990, 850, 810)
3. terms/ - General terminology (Stops, Route Optimization, Accessorials, Demurrage, SCAC)
4. parties/ - Stakeholders (Shipper, Carrier, Consignee, Forwarder, Broker, 3PL)
5. locations/ - Geographic info (Address Formats, Ports, Terminals, Distribution Centers)
6. packaging/ - Handling units (Pallets, Containers, Crates, Drums)
7. financials/ - Cost structures (FTL Charges, LTL Rates, Accessorial Charges, Fuel Surcharges)

# Placement Logic:
- HOW freight moves? → modes/
- X12 transaction? → edi/
- WHO (stakeholder)? → parties/
- WHERE (location)? → locations/
- Packaging type? → packaging/
- Cost/billing? → financials/
- Otherwise → terms/

# Naming Rules:

## General:
- Extension: .md
- Simple terms: no spaces (use PascalCase)
- Compound industry terms: preserve spaces
- Match official capitalization

## By Category:
- edi/: [code].md (e.g., 997.md, 204.md)
- modes/: [ModeName].md (e.g., LessThanTruckLoad.md)
- terms/: [Term Name].md (e.g., Route Optimization.md)
- parties/: [PartyRole].md (e.g., Customs Broker.md)
- locations/: [LocationType].md (e.g., Formats.md)
- packaging/: [Unit Name].md (e.g., Handling Units.md)
- financials/: [Cost Type].md (e.g., FTL Charges)

## Special:
- Avoid: / \ : * ? " < > |
- Each category has README.md
- Root has README.md entry point

# Primary Standards:

1. NMFTA (nmfta.org) - Motor carrier, SCAC codes, classifications
2. ANSI X12 (x12.org) - EDI transaction standards
3. IATA (iata.org) - Air freight standards
4. IMO (imo.org) - Ocean shipping regulations

# Secondary:
- Carrier documentation (FedEx, UPS, USPS)
- Trade associations (IANA, TIA)
- Government agencies (DOT, CBP)

# Process:
1. Check primary standards body
2. If not found, check carrier/association docs
3. If conflicts, note discrepancy
4. Always cite source with URL
5. Prefer recent publications

# Prohibited:
- Wikipedia (verify with authoritative source)
- General dictionaries
- Blog posts
- Outdated docs (>5 years)

skills.name: doc-entry
skills.description: Standard workflow for adding new documentation entries to FrieghtKB
skills.content:
# Documentation Entry Workflow

## Steps:
1. Identify category: Determine which top-level folder (modes/, edi/, terms/, parties/, locations/, packaging/, financials/)
2. Create file: Use PascalCase for multi-word files
3. Apply template: H1 title, Definition paragraph, Key Attributes section, Related Terms section, References section
4. Verify terminology: Cross-check against NMFTA/ANSI standards
5. Link bidirectionally: Update related entries to link back
6. Commit with format: Create [TermName].md

## Quality checks:
- File in correct category folder
- Industry terms properly capitalized
- At least 2 related terms linked
- At least 1 authoritative reference

skills.name: edi-doc
skills.description: Specialized workflow for documenting EDI transaction sets
skills.content:
# EDI Documentation Workflow

## Mandatory sections:
1. Transaction Code: X12 number
2. Official Name: ANSI X12 standard name
3. Purpose: Business workflow role
4. Direction: Sender to Receiver
5. Required Fields: Mandatory segments table
6. Optional Fields: Common optional segments
7. Business Scenarios: 2-3 examples
8. Related Transactions: Workflow chain links

## Naming:
- File: [code].md
- Title: EDI [code] - [name]

## References:
- Link to ANSI X12 documentation
- Include implementation guide URL

skills.name: category-expand
skills.description: Process for adding new documentation categories
skills.content:
# Category Expansion Process

## Before adding:
1. Check if fits existing 7 categories
2. Verify at least 5 entries justify new category
3. Propose in issue/discussion

## If approved:
1. Create directory with README.md
2. README includes: purpose, scope, entry criteria, naming conventions
3. Update root README.md
4. Seed with 3 initial entries
5. Update related entries with cross-links

## Commit: Add [category]/ with [n] entries

skills.name: link-check
skills.content:
# Link Validation Workflow

## Check types:
1. Internal links resolve
2. Category backlinks present
3. Bidirectional related terms
4. External references HTTP 200

## Fix process:
1. Update moved file paths
2. Add missing backlinks
3. Replace dead URLs with alternatives
4. Document in commit message

## Commit: Fix broken links in [category]/

skills.name: term-deprecate
skills.content:
# Term Deprecation Workflow

## When outdated:
1. Keep file for history
2. Add deprecation notice at top
3. Update incoming links to replacement
4. Add redirect in category README
5. Remove from main navigation

## Retention:
- Keep 1 year
- Then move to archive/
- Never delete if externally referenced

## Commit: Deprecate [OldTerm] in favor of [NewTerm]

skills.name: i18n-doc
skills.content:
# Internationalization Workflow

## Supported regions:
- Primary: English (US)
- Variants: Canada, Mexico, EU, Asia-Pacific

## Adding variant:
1. File naming: [Term]_[region].md
2. Include standard template sections
3. Add Region field
4. Highlight Regional Differences section
5. Link to base and other variants

## When to create:
- Terminology differs significantly
- Legal/regulatory requirements differ
- Industry practices vary
- NOT for minor spelling differences
